clue.text: He often scored century, like a star

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
as means like, in the sense of 'in the manner of'
a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness

explanation.surface: A cricketer who regularly made hundreds and was treated like a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' suggests runs or goals, but here it is the slang sense of a seduction; 'century' looks like cricket too.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova was the famous Venetian seducer, so his name stands for any man with many romantic conquests.

clue.text: Scores piece, finale from Debussy

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its closing letter, so take the end of Debussy

explanation.surface: A section of a composition, perhaps the closing movement of a Debussy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks musical, as does 'piece', but it means lots, a great many.
explanation.definitionFit: Scores of things are a large number of them, which is what many means.

clue.text: He rapidly scored a second, with variable skill

parts.note: mo is a short moment, as in 'wait a mo'
z is a standard algebraic symbol for an unknown variable
art means skill, as in 'the art of persuasion'

explanation.surface: A footballer struck quickly, a second goal, showing unpredictable skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' here means wrote music; Mozart was famously quick at composing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart composed with legendary speed, writing whole works out apparently without revision.

clue.text: Wearing old hat, perform material

indicators.note: the hat word is put on over the perform word, so it surrounds it

parts.note: tile is dated British slang for a hat
to act is to perform on stage

explanation.surface: An actor puts on a dated hat to perform a piece of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like 'outdated' but is the slang TILE; 'material' is the adjective meaning physical, not cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tactile can be touched, which is to say it is physical or material rather than abstract.

clue.text: Theatrical love movie set around eastern desert

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: the movie word is placed around the next two pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
to rat is to desert or betray one's side

explanation.surface: A romantic film shot in a desert in the east, with lots of drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a sandy setting for the film, but it is the verb, giving RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic behaviour is extravagantly dramatic, like an opera, hence theatrical.

clue.text: Shows impatience, admitting tramp doesn't know the score?

indicators.note: letting someone in, so the impatience word takes the tramp word inside it

parts.note: someone who sighs is showing impatience
to tramp is to tread heavily

explanation.surface: Someone sighs impatiently while having to let a vagrant in, out of touch with events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't know the score' is an idiom for being uninformed; here a musician who sight-reads plays music not seen before. 'Tramp' is the verb, not the vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight-reader performs music on first sight, literally without prior knowledge of the written music.

clue.text: Create a vibrato effect as part of a score

definitions.meaning: to sing or sound with a trembling voice
an eighth note in written music

explanation.surface: A musician adds vibrato while playing a passage of the music.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaver is both a trembling of the voice and the eighth-note symbol in musical notation.

clue.text: Name-dropping singer covers half of aria he scored manually

indicators.note: the trimmed singer's name wraps around the other piece
dropping means losing, so the abbreviation for name is taken out of the singer

parts.note: Madonna is the pop singer

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A star singer, despite name-dropping, covers part of an aria in a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manually' recalls Maradona's 'Hand of God' goal for Argentina against England in 1986, punched in with his hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego Maradona famously put the ball into the net with his hand at the 1986 World Cup.

clue.text: It's used to cook proper cuts evenly

parts.note: prim means proper or primly correct

indicators.note: taking the even-numbered letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A chef's tool for making neat, even cuts properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts evenly' sounds like a kitchen knife; it gives the second and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Primus is a brand of portable paraffin stove, used for cooking on camping trips.

clue.text: A bit dirty, caught in some light

indicators.note: the caught letter sits inside the light word

parts.note: a ray is a beam, some light
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Something slightly grubby is spotted in a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy jokes are mildly risqué, so a bit dirty in the sense of suggestive.

clue.text: Enjoy following sweet scent

indicators.note: the enjoy word comes after the sweet word

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, a sweet
to have is to enjoy, as in having a good time

explanation.surface: Savour a pleasant scent after a sugary course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for 'scent'; it is the noun meaning pudding, AFTERS in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a perfumed lotion men apply after shaving, so a kind of fragrance.

clue.text: Amazing score Tchaikovsky's beginning — it may take your breath away!

definitions.text: it may take your breath away!

indicators.note: amazing here suggests the letters are thrown into confusion, rearranged
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A wonderful Tchaikovsky score, opening thrillingly, leaves the listener breathless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take your breath away' usually means stunning; a tight corset literally restricts breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a tightly laced undergarment that constricts the waist, notoriously making breathing hard.

clue.text: Score synthetic meth and use thus

indicators.note: synthetic means artificially made, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: Buy man-made methamphetamine and take it this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug picture is a decoy; the definition is the written music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical score is printed sheet music, the notated parts for performers.

clue.text: Computing bores rarely represented in books

indicators.note: the computing letters bore into, so they sit inside, the rearranged word
re-presented, offered in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: IT is information technology, computing

explanation.surface: People who talk about computing are seldom found in books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' looks like a noun for tedious people; it is a verb meaning drills into.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary means relating to literature, so to do with what appears in books.

clue.text: Welcomed in dugout, a venerable English scorer

indicators.note: the answer is taken in, sitting within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A respected English goalscorer is received warmly in the dugout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' looks footballing, but it means composer; Sir John Tavener wrote 'The Protecting Veil'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Tavener was an English composer, someone who writes musical scores.

clue.text: Tries to cut peonies periodically put in black vehicle

indicators.note: the tries word cuts into the letters picked from the flowers
taking letters at regular intervals, here the even-numbered ones

parts.note: a judge hears, or tries, a case

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to cut peonies now and then for a funeral car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like attempts; it is the legal sense, a judge hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhearse is to place a body in a hearse, the black car used at funerals.

clue.text: Score that's zero for golfer

definitions.meaning: to score a mark on a surface
a ... golfer plays off a handicap of zero

explanation.surface: A golfer whose score shows no handicap at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratch means both to mark with a line and, in golf, a handicap of nothing.

clue.text: Composed score without previous blemish

indicators.note: in the old sense outside, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
composed means put together, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: old means former or previous, as in 'my old school'

explanation.surface: A composer wrote a score without using the earlier one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'Composed' looks like calm but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold sore is a small blister near the lips, a skin blemish caused by herpes.

clue.text: They try to score total: it's divided by a hundred

parts.note: to add is to total up

indicators.note: split apart by, so the hundred letter goes into the middle

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Players trying to reach a total that gets split by a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' here is slang for obtaining illegal drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug addicts are always looking to buy drugs, which in slang is to score.

clue.text: What sewer did in street caused irritation

parts.note: something that itched caused irritation to the skin

explanation.surface: Something in the road caused annoyance at the drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain, but it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sews works with needle and thread, and the past action is that they stitched.

clue.text: Score which is doubled in cricket

definitions.meaning: ...20 is the short form of cricket, its name doubling the number

explanation.surface: A number that gets doubled in a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A score traditionally means twenty, and Twenty20 is the short cricket format named by repeating it.

clue.text: Score from one of the 19 backing officer

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: 19 down is ADDICTS, and a drug addict is a user
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A goal comes from one of the team who supports an official.
explanation.definitionFit: The score of a match is its result, the final outcome.

clue.text: French scorer has butter and drink at home

parts.note: a ram is an animal that butts
eau is French for water, the drink in the composer's home country

explanation.surface: A French striker has butter and a drink at his own house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is a thing that butts, not the dairy spread. Jean-Philippe Rameau was a French Baroque composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rameau was an eighteenth-century French composer, a writer of musical scores.

clue.text: What could make us calmer is a worldly notion

indicators.note: the letters could be made into the answer by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Something that might soothe us is a down-to-earth idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Secularism is the doctrine that public life should be free of religion, a this-worldly principle.

clue.text: Top scorer (on and off the pitch)

definitions.meaning: George ..., the Manchester United footballer, scored goals and was a notorious womaniser

explanation.surface: The leading goalscorer, both during matches and away from them.
explanation.walkthrough: George Best was a Northern Irish footballing star famous for his playboy lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Best means finest, top; George Best scored freely in football and in romance.

clue.text: Set of loaves? With no time, he produced scores

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: a batch is a set of loaves baked together

explanation.surface: A baker without time still turned out numerous loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian Bach was a hugely prolific German composer of musical works.

clue.text: What 8 and 24 put on vessel about to set off

indicators.note: around, so the vessel letters go around the other piece

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to trip an alarm is to set it off

explanation.surface: Two footballers board a ship that is about to depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 across MARADONA and 24 across BEST were footballers, who wear team strips, the British term for kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip is a football team's kit, which players put on for a match.

clue.text: Spooner's to stuff seamen in transport

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial consonants change places

parts.note: to cram is to stuff
tars is slang for sailors

explanation.surface: Spooner wants to pack sailors into a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramcars are street trams, a form of public transport.
